paper.title_en: Interpreting the HI 21-cm cosmology maps through Largest Cluster Statistics III: Impact of the lightcone effect
paper.abstract_en: The redshifted 21-cm signal emitted by neutral Hydrogen (HI) is a promising probe to understand the evolution of the topology of ionized regions during the Epoch of Reionization (EoR). The topology of ionized regions allows us to infer the nature and properties of ionizing sources, i.e., early galaxies and AGNs. Traditional Fourier statistics, such as the power spectrum, help us quantify the strength of fluctuations in this field at different length scales but do not preserve its phase information. Analyzing the 21-cm brightness temperature field in the image domain retains its non-Gaussian characteristics and morphological information. One such approach is to track the coalescence of multiple ionized regions to form one contiguous ionized region spanning the universe. This is referred to as percolation, and its onset is quantified by a sharp rise in the value of the Largest Cluster Statistic (LCS) approaching unity. In this work, we carry out a percolation analysis of 21-cm brightness temperature maps by studying the redshift evolution of the LCS along a lightcone to distinguish between several simulated reionization scenarios. We estimate the LCS of subvolumes of different sizes in mock SKA-Low 21-cm lightcone maps and study their redshift evolution for different reionization scenarios using a moving volume approach. We find that the optimal size of the moving volume that reproduces the percolation transition from coeval maps varies across reionization scenarios and the evolution of LCS remains distinct across the reionization scenarios for a fixed moving volume bandwidth. The inferred percolation transition strongly depends on the synthesized beam width and the percentage gain calibration error, and is tractable for an optimistic SKA-Low observational setup.
